sources.title: Cuba Travel: Regulations for traveling to Cuba
sources.officialityEvidence: The current Cuban tourism portal supplies the national tourist entry requirements, names China’s regular-passport exemption, and directs tourist-visa applicants to eVisaCuba.
sources.supportingExcerpt: Tourist visas via internet, which replaces the current Tourist Card.

sources.title: eVisa-Cuba tourist visa service
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Cuba
sources.officialityEvidence: The live eVisa service identifies the Cuban Foreign Ministry in its footer and provides application and visa-verification functions.
sources.supportingExcerpt: You will receive a response within the next 72 business hours.

sources.title: eVisa-Cuba: Apply for electronic visa
sources.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Cuba
sources.officialityEvidence: The live Cuban Foreign Ministry eVisa application page collects passport and nationality data for an electronic tourist-visa application.

policies.title: Chinese regular passport: Cuba tourist-visa exemption
policies.summary: Cuba Travel expressly exempts Chinese citizens using a regular passport from Cuba’s tourist-visa requirement.
conditions: This applies to Chinese nationals travelling with a regular passport for the short-tourist baseline. Cuba Travel gives tourist stays of up to 90 days, extendable once for 90 more days.

A valid passport, D’VIAJEROS QR code, medical insurance, return ticket, health/security checks and final admission remain applicable. Work, residence, transit, special passports and individual restrictions are excluded.
The electronic tourist-visa system replaces the Tourist Card for visa-required tourist applicants; this exemption is not normalized as eVisa.
